clue.text: Sanctimonious old tyrant who won acclaim as a dramatist

parts.note: pi is crossword slang for pious or sanctimonious
Nero was the notoriously cruel Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A self-righteous former despot somehow found a second career writing hit plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Wing Pinero was a celebrated Victorian and Edwardian playwright; 'who won acclaim as a' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Pinero was an English playwright, author of The Magistrate and other successful stage comedies.

clue.text: A girl men guilefully order to swing the lead, apparently

indicators.note: to order letters guilefully is to arrange them craftily into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written, eight letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A girl craftily bosses men about so she can dodge work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swing the lead' is a British idiom for shirking work by pretending to be ill; 'apparently' signals the pretence.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirking duty by feigning sickness is exactly what the idiom about swinging the lead describes.

clue.text: Just printed a description of what the freshly ironed clothes were?

definitions.text: a description of what the freshly ironed clothes were?

explanation.surface: Newly printed news, and laundry fresh off the ironing board.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a newspaper idiom for something just off the presses; literally, clothes just pressed with a hot iron are warm from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Newly run off a printing machine is the idiom's sense; laundry just smoothed by a hot iron is literally warm from the pressing.

clue.text: A female science graduate posing a drainage problem operationally?

parts.note: BSc is a Bachelor of Science degree
-ess is the suffix marking a female, as in lioness or actress

explanation.surface: A woman with a science degree presents a puzzle about plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: The female is the suffix -ESS, placed after the graduate. 'Drainage problem operationally' means a pus-filled swelling a surgeon must drain, not a blocked pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pus-filled swelling often needs surgical draining, so medically it is a drainage problem.

clue.text: The notes to the play, maybe

definitions.text: The notes to the play, maybe

parts.words: The notes to the play, maybe
parts.note: reads like programme notes accompanying a drama, but the notes are musical ones played alongside a stage production

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the written notes in a theatre programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Background score written to accompany a stage drama is what the musical notes to a play would be.

clue.text: A striking deed of minor devilry?

parts.note: an imp is a minor devil, the agent of small mischief
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: Asks whether a remarkable deed was really just a bit of mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: The deed of an imp reads as IMP ACT, with the possessor first; 'striking' is the noun, a blow or collision.
explanation.definitionFit: A collision or forceful blow is a striking in the noun sense.

clue.text: Furry creature that has a lot of weight to carry

definitions.text: Furry creature that has a lot of weight to carry

parts.words: Furry creature that has a lot of weight to carry
parts.note: describes a big heavy furry animal, while the verb form means to carry or support a load

explanation.surface: A heavy furry animal lumbers along under its own bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: The large furry mammal shares its name with the verb meaning to carry or support a load.

clue.text: Proud possessor of a listed building

definitions.text: Proud possessor of a listed building

parts.words: Proud possessor of a listed building
parts.note: a listed building in Britain is a protected historic one, but here listed means leaning, as a ship lists

explanation.surface: A town boasts of owning a protected historic building.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'listed' building is one protected for its historic value; a ship that 'lists' leans over, and this city's famous tower leans.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city owns the famous Leaning Tower, a building that tilts like a ship listing.

clue.text: The royal round!

parts.note: a round object carried as part of the royal regalia, the jewelled sphere topped with a cross

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a round of drinks bought by royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: The sovereign's jewelled sphere, part of the crown regalia, is a round royal object.

clue.text: Comparatively insensitive figure?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is rather unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as numb-er, it is the comparative of numb; read normally, it is a figure such as 7.
explanation.definitionFit: More lacking in feeling is the comparative of numb; a digit or numeral is a figure.

clue.text: Kind of map to which the underprivileged are entitled

definitions.text: to which the underprivileged are entitled

explanation.surface: A note on cartography and on welfare for the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a map showing hills and valleys by shading; the other is aid given to the poor, as in poor relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A map showing height and terrain is a contour type; aid or welfare given to those in need is the other sense.

clue.text: Courteous consideration for the weak larch entwined with ivy?

indicators.note: ivy twisting round a tree mixes the two, so their letters are wound together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A larch with ivy twined round it, the strong supporting the weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entwined' scrambles LARCH and IVY together; 'with' joins them. The surface pictures the tree gallantly holding up the climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The knightly code of protecting the vulnerable and showing gallant courtesy is the definition's sense.

clue.text: Splendid conditions for the holiday season

definitions.text: Splendid conditions for the holiday season

parts.words: Splendid conditions for the holiday season
parts.note: conditions here means the state of sun, rain and wind, and splendid means lovely, the hope for a summer break

explanation.surface: A wish for perfect circumstances during summer holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovely sunny days are the splendid climate everyone hopes for on a summer break.

clue.text: Her woollen coat protects her from the weather

definitions.text: Her woollen coat protects her from the weather

parts.words: Her woollen coat protects her from the weather
parts.note: sounds like a woman in a wool overcoat, but the coat is the fleece of a female sheep

explanation.surface: A woman wraps up in her wool coat against the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep grows a woollen fleece that keeps out rain and cold.

clue.text: A fertiliser container returned with speed

indicators.note: returned means the word for the container is read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a container
a rate is a speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A bag of fertiliser is sent back quickly in its container.
explanation.definitionFit: Salts of nitric acid are widely spread on fields as fertiliser.

clue.text: She is decidedly awkward initially

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A woman is described as being very difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands for a female person, here referred to as she.

clue.text: Brought to a halt, as the oxen were at the end of the day

definitions.text: as the oxen were at the end of the day

explanation.surface: Something stops, like farm animals being shut away for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is stopped; the other is put in a stall, a shed compartment for livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopped or halted is one sense; housed in a stall in a cowshed is the other.

clue.text: Predatory bird found in countries that lie at the foot of mountains

definitions.text: that lie at the foot of mountains

indicators.note: found in places the bird inside the word for countries

parts.note: lands are countries
an owl is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A hunting bird lives in regions below the mountain slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'countries' too: these are the low-lying regions below high ground, such as the Scottish Lowlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat low-lying regions are found below hills and mountains, as opposed to highlands.

clue.text: In no position to get in a shot

definitions.text: In no position to get in a shot

parts.words: In no position to get in a shot
parts.note: sounds like a person badly placed, but in football a player ahead of the ball in an illegal place cannot score

explanation.surface: Someone is badly placed to take a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: In football (soccer), a player in this position when the ball is played to them is penalised, so cannot legitimately shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A football player caught ahead of the last defender is illegally placed and may not take a shot.

clue.text: A blooming fight at the Mardi Gras celebrations in Nice

definitions.text: A blooming fight at the Mardi Gras celebrations in Nice

parts.words: A blooming fight at the Mardi Gras celebrations in Nice
parts.note: blooming reads as a mild British swear word, but the fight is literally with blooms, thrown at the carnival on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A bloody brawl breaks out during the carnival in Nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' is mild British slang for 'bloody'; Nice's carnival really does hold a parade where blossoms are thrown at the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nice carnival's parade where floats pelt spectators with blossoms is a fight fought with blooms.

clue.text: Sums lost at rummy?

indicators.note: rummy is British slang for odd or strange, so the letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks how much money was lost playing the card game rummy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rummy' looks like the card game but is British slang for odd, scrambling LOST and AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sums are added-up amounts, the figures at the bottom of a column.

clue.text: He edges round the mischievous jackdaw's domicile

indicators.note: the word for edges goes round the pronoun, enclosing it

parts.note: rims are edges
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man moves round the edges of a place where a naughty bird lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jackdaw of Rheims is a comic poem in the Ingoldsby Legends about a bird that steals a cardinal's ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The French cathedral city is home to the thieving bird in the famous Ingoldsby Legends poem.

clue.text: Not the news items on the face of it!

explanation.surface: Remarks on newspaper articles and on someone's looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Newspapers carry feature articles as well as news reports; a face has eyes, nose and mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Longer magazine-style articles in a newspaper are distinct from news; eyes, nose and mouth are what make up a face.

clue.text: One test out of a thousand?

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex libris
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Asks whether one trial was chosen from a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or university paper sat under timed conditions is a test.

clue.text: Customs that give us lots of time eventually

parts.note: ages means a long time, as in I waited for ages

explanation.surface: Traditions that eventually reward us with plenty of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitual practices or conventions are customs, the established ways of doing things.

clue.text: Sad reflection about everything shown on television.

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the other piece
a reflection in a mirror reverses, so the word sad is read backwards

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A sorrowful look back at everything broadcast on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' turns SAD into DAS, and 'about' puts that around ALL. The definition points to the long-running American TV soap set in Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Texan oil-family soap opera was a long-running television series, so it was famously broadcast on TV.

clue.text: The Welsh lad 16 transformed

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of the other answer are rearranged into a new word

parts.note: 16 refers to the answer of clue 16 down

explanation.surface: A Welsh boy changes into a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 16 down is IDA; 'transformed' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Welsh nickname, short for David, is a typical name for a Welsh boy.

clue.text: Superior vault that is built to look round

definitions.text: Superior vault that is built to look round

parts.words: Superior vault that is built to look round
parts.note: a vault overhead, built rounded, the superior or upper curved roof of a building

explanation.surface: A grand arched ceiling designed to appear circular.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded hemispherical roof is a vault raised high over a building, circular in plan.
